answer_1.quote: We use GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) as our default backbone model M for code generation and decomposition... We conduct experiments with the problems from two widely adopted competition-level code generation benchmarks, namely APPS and Code-Contests.
answer_1.outputs: decomposed code solutions (functions/subtasks) and repaired program implementations

answer_2.quote: Metric We measure the supervision quality in competitive programming by programs' passing rates on unit test cases. Specifically, we aggregate the program's performance on test cases with two metrics. Test Case Average Accuracy computes the average fraction of test cases passed among all the test cases. Strict Accuracy computes the average fraction of programs that pass all test cases.

answer_3.quote: We evaluate the effectiveness of our ranking model π_rank in predicting the assistive value of decompositions. We construct paired decompositions annotated with real assistive value labels as the test data. The results shown in Table indicate that LLMs can learn to select higher-AssistV decomposition for assisting humans via in-context learning.

answer_4.quote: We recruit 30 Python programmers, including 11 experts and 19 non-experts, to repair model-generated program solutions for competitive coding problems, resulting in a total of 177 worker hours... We measure the time required to collect repaired programs with 68% test case accuracy and compare it across conditions.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators repaired generated programs and were evaluated on repair time and test case accuracy (average and strict).
